newsitem.title: GREECE: Wave of labour strikes threaten to cripple Greece.
newsitem.headline: Wave of labour strikes threaten to cripple Greece.

text.p: A wave of nationwide 24-hour labour strikes in protest against Greece's new austerity budget threatened to cripple public services, transport and industries on Thursday.

Greece's trade union federation, the General Confederation of Greek Workers (GSEE) with some three million members, has called the walkout to protest against the strict budget, which is expected to be presented in parliament on Friday.

The union of civil servants ADEDY has joined the strike, threatening to close down all public services for the day. Banks, ministries, hospitals, schools, transport and shops are also expected to be affected.
Olympic Airways, the national carrier, will stage a three-hour stoppage from 0600 gmt, which might cause flight delays.

Farmers have also announced they will hold rallies to press for higher prices for their produce and they could put up roadblocks on national highways, cutting off the main artery connecting Athens with the northern city of Salonika.
Trade union federation GSEE and civil servants union have planned a rally in central Athens on Thursday morning, followed by a march to the national economy ministry and parliament.
The tough budget includes the abolition of most tax breaks and cuts in state spending in order to meet targets set by the European Union's Maastricht treaty.
Greece is the only EU country that has failed to meet any of the criteria for joining economic and monetary union (EMU).
The socialist government has said it is determined to push through its tough budget and incomes policy to close the big gap between Greece and its EU partners.
